title: Standard parabolic Levi root data and Zariski torsor charts
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a semisimple $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], where semisimple means smooth, connected, affine and of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup. Solvable means that successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups become trivial. Choose a split maximal torus $T\subseteq B_0\subseteq G$ with $B_0$ a Borel subgroup, and write $(X,\Phi,X_*,\Phi^\vee)$, $\Phi_0^+$ and $\Delta_0$ for its root datum, positive roots and simple roots [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For every root $\gamma$, let $U_\gamma$ be the root subgroup [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. For any subset $I\subseteq\Delta_0$, let $\Phi_I=\Phi\cap\mathbf Z I$, let $T_I$ be the largest subtorus of $\bigcap_{\beta\in I}\ker(\beta)$, and put $L_I=C_G(T_I)$, where the centralizer consists of elements commuting with $T_I$ after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Let $P_I$ be the closed subgroup generated by $B_0$ and the subgroups $U_{-\beta}$ for $\beta\in I$. Then $P_I$ is smooth and connected and the quotient $G/P_I$ representing the fppf right-coset sheaf is a proper finite-type $F$-scheme. Here fppf coverings are jointly surjective flat finitely presented coverings. The group $L_I$ is reductive, contains $T$ as a split maximal torus, and has root datum $(X,\Phi_I,X_*,\{\gamma^\vee:\gamma\in\Phi_I\})$. The intersection $B_I=B_0\cap L_I$ is a Borel subgroup of $L_I$ with positive roots $\Phi_I\cap\Phi_0^+$. The unipotent radical $R_I$ of $P_I$ is generated by the $U_\gamma$ with $\gamma\in\Phi_0^+\setminus\Phi_I$, and multiplication induces isomorphisms
$$R_I\rtimes L_I\xrightarrow{\sim}P_I,\qquad R_I\rtimes B_I\xrightarrow{\sim}B_0.$$
The unipotent radical is the largest smooth connected normal subgroup all of whose geometric points are unipotent in a faithful matrix representation; $u$ is unipotent if $(u-1)^n=0$ for some $n$. The semidirect products have the conjugation action and underlying schemes given by products. The map $G\to G/P_I$ is a right $P_I$-torsor and has a finite Zariski open covering with regular sections; a right torsor means a faithfully flat finitely presented map with $G\times_F P_I\cong G\times_{G/P_I}G$ by $(g,p)\mapsto(g,gp)$. No characteristic restriction or simply connectedness hypothesis is imposed, and $I=\varnothing$ and $I=\Delta_0$ are allowed.

source.place: Notation 21.89, Proposition 21.90 and Theorem 21.91, printed pp.453--454 (root subsystem, Levi and radical); Theorem 17.16, printed p.356 (proper parabolic quotient); Theorem 25.9(a), printed pp.545--546, using Theorem 13.33(d), printed p.265 (local sections). The Borel semidirect product is the restriction of the displayed radical-root description. The torsor is Section 18c, p.390; a finite subcover exists because the quotient is quasi-compact.

proof.text: The semisimple group $G$ is reductive by [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. By [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span] and [lem-sfb-root-base-rational-integral-spans], $\Delta_0$ is a basis of $X\otimes\mathbf Q$. Take its rational dual vectors $\eta_\beta\in X_*\otimes\mathbf Q$ and clear denominators in $\sum_{\beta\notin I}\eta_\beta$. This gives an actual cocharacter $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to T$ and an integer $d>0$ with $\langle\beta,\lambda\rangle=0$ on $I$ and $d$ on $\Delta_0\setminus I$. If $I=\Delta_0$, take $\lambda=0$ and $d=1$. Writing a root $\gamma=\sum c_\beta\beta$, the coefficients have one sign, so $\langle\gamma,\lambda\rangle=0$ exactly when $\gamma\in\Phi_I$; positive roots outside $\Phi_I$ have strictly positive pairing.

source.place: 21.88, printed p.452 (rational fundamental cocharacters); Corollary 21.92, p.455

proof.text: Write $M=\mathbf Z I\subseteq X$ and $M^{\mathrm{sat}}=X\cap(M\otimes\mathbf Q)$. The character antiduality of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] describes $D=\bigcap_{\beta\in I}\ker\beta$ as the diagonalizable group with character group $X/M$: in $F[X]$ its equations are $e_\beta=1$. Its subgroup with character quotient $X/M^{\mathrm{sat}}$ is a torus. Every subtorus of $D$ factors through it, because a map from $X/M$ to a free abelian character group kills torsion. It is therefore the largest subtorus $T_I$ of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus]. Thus $\gamma|_{T_I}=1$ if and only if $\gamma\in M\otimes\mathbf Q$, which for roots is equivalent to $\gamma\in\Phi_I$ by uniqueness of the integral simple-root coordinates. Also $\lambda$ factors through $T_I$: the map on characters kills $M$, hence its saturation, since $\mathbf Z$ is torsion free.

source.place: Notation 21.89(c) and proof of Proposition 21.90(a), p.453; Theorems 12.9 and 12.23, pp.232--234,240

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-fixed-subgroup] to $T_I\subseteq G$. It gives a reductive smooth connected closed subgroup $L=C_G(T_I)$. The inclusion $T\subseteq L$ follows because $T$ is commutative; it is maximal in $L$ because it was maximal in $G$. The centralizer equation on dual numbers says exactly that $\operatorname{Lie}(L)=\operatorname{Lie}(G)^{T_I}$. The character weight decomposition of [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] and step 2 therefore give
$$\operatorname{Lie}(L)=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus\bigoplus_{\gamma\in\Phi_I}\mathfrak g_\gamma.$$
Here invariance uses torus characters on all algebras, not their derivatives. For $\gamma\in\Phi_I$ the root-subgroup conjugation formula of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] shows $U_\gamma\subseteq L$. Applying the same node to the reductive pair $(L,T)$ identifies its root subgroup with this $U_\gamma$, by the stated uniqueness for its tangent space.

source.place: Proposition 21.90(a), p.453; Corollary 17.59, p.371; Theorem 21.11, pp.428--430

proof.text: The character and cocharacter lattices of $(L,T)$ are $X,X_*$ because the torus has not changed. For $\gamma\in\Phi_I$ let $T_\gamma$ be the largest subtorus of $\ker\gamma$. Since $\gamma|_{T_I}=1$, $T_I\subseteq T_\gamma$, hence $G_\gamma=C_G(T_\gamma)\subseteq L$. The rank-one subgroup for $\gamma$ computed inside $L$ is consequently $C_L(T_\gamma)=G_\gamma$. The rank-one construction and uniqueness in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], applied in both groups, give the same cocharacter $\gamma^\vee$: it is the diagonal-torus map of the same rank-one $\operatorname{SL}_2$ homomorphism. This proves the entire asserted root datum, including the ambient coroots, rather than merely equality of root sets.

By [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-borel-intersection], $B_I=B_0\cap L$ is a Borel subgroup of $L$. Its tangent space is the intersection of the two tangent spaces (evaluate their fibre product on dual numbers). By [lem-sfb-borel-opposite-root-dichotomy] and step 3 its positive roots are exactly $\Phi_I\cap\Phi_0^+$. Their simple-root base is $I$: each of these positive roots has nonnegative integral coefficients supported in $I$, and the elements of $I$ are linearly independent and cannot be sums of two positive roots. Thus the simple-root generation statement of [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation] applies to $L$ with this base.

Apply [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] to $\lambda$ and denote its groups by $P_\lambda,U_\lambda,Z_\lambda$. They are smooth connected closed subgroups and $P_\lambda=U_\lambda\rtimes Z_\lambda$. Since $\lambda$ factors through $T_I$, $L\subseteq Z_\lambda$. By the cocharacter tangent formula, step 1 and [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], $\operatorname{Lie}(Z_\lambda)$ is spanned by $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$ and the $\mathfrak g_\gamma$ with $\gamma\in\Phi_I$. The smooth connected subgroups $T$ and $U_\gamma$ lie in $L$ and their tangent spaces span this space. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation] in $Z_\lambda$ with closed subgroup $L$. It yields $L=Z_\lambda$, as subgroup schemes.

source.place: Theorem 13.33(a)--(c),(e), pp.265--266; Proposition 21.90(a), p.453; Corollary 21.92, p.455

proof.text: Put $S=\Phi_0^+\setminus\Phi_I$. For $\gamma\in S$, the conjugation formula in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] is $\lambda(t)u_\gamma(a)\lambda(t)^{-1}=u_\gamma(t^{\langle\gamma,\lambda\rangle}a)$; its exponent is positive. Thus $U_\gamma\subseteq U_\lambda$ as functors on all algebras. For any ordering of $S$, multiplication $\prod_{\gamma\in S}U_\gamma\to U_\lambda$ is $\lambda$-equivariant. Its differential is the direct sum of the one-dimensional root spaces, hence an isomorphism by [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] and the tangent formula of [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure]. Source and target are smooth connected affine schemes with strictly positive integer tangent weights. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-weight-equivariant-inverse]; multiplication is an isomorphism. In particular $U_\lambda$ is generated by exactly these root subgroups, and $S=\varnothing$ gives $U_\lambda=1$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 21.91, p.454; Theorem 21.68(a), p.445; Corollary 13.42, p.270

proof.text: Every positive root has nonnegative pairing with $\lambda$, so its root subgroup is in $P_\lambda$ by the same explicit extension formula; $T\subseteq Z_\lambda$. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates] and the decomposition $B_0=R_u(B_0)\rtimes T$ in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], this proves $B_0\subseteq P_\lambda$. Order the positive roots outside $\Phi_I$ first, followed by those inside. Apply the root-product node in $G$ and in the reductive group $L$ with Borel $B_I$. Together with step 7 these product coordinates identify $U_\lambda\times_F B_I\to B_0$ with an isomorphism of schemes. Since $U_\lambda$ is normal in $P_\lambda$ and $B_I\subseteq L$, its group law is the displayed conjugation semidirect-product law. Hence $B_0=U_\lambda\rtimes B_I$.

source.place: Theorem 21.68(a), p.445; Proposition 21.90 and proof of Theorem 21.91, pp.453--454

proof.text: Let $K$ be any closed subgroup containing $B_0$ and every $U_{-\beta}$ for $\beta\in I$. It contains $T$ and $U_{\pm\beta}$ for $\beta\in I$, so $K\cap L=L$ by [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation] applied to $(L,T,B_I)$. It also contains $U_\lambda$ by step 8. Therefore the isomorphism $U_\lambda\rtimes L\simeq P_\lambda$ of [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] factors through $K$. Conversely $P_\lambda$ contains $B_0$ and each $U_{-\beta}$ for $\beta\in I$ (the latter lies in $L$ by step 3). This is precisely the universal property of the closed subgroup generated in the question, so $P_I=P_\lambda$. In particular $P_I$ is smooth and connected.

source.place: Theorem 21.91 and its proof, pp.453--454; Corollary 21.92, p.455

proof.text: The group $U_\lambda$ is smooth connected normal and unipotent by [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure]. To show it is the full unipotent radical, let $N$ be any smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup of $P_I$. The projection $f:P_I=U_\lambda\rtimes L\to L$ is faithfully flat: factor it by [lem-sfb-affine-homomorphism-flat-image]; its closed image is all of $L$ because $f$ has the section $L\hookrightarrow P_I$. Factor $f|_N$ by the same node. By [lem-sfb-unipotent-normal-quotient-image], its closed image in $L$ is smooth connected normal and unipotent. Since $L$ is reductive, that image is trivial. Thus $N\subseteq\ker f=U_\lambda$. This proves $R_I=U_\lambda$, so steps 6--8 give both claimed semidirect products and the claimed radical generators.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 21.91, p.454; Corollary 14.7, p.282; Theorem 3.34, p.75

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] to the smooth connected affine group $G$ and closed subgroup $P_I$. It represents the fppf right-coset sheaf by a separated finite-type $F$-scheme $Q=G/P_I$, and gives $G\times_FP_I\simeq G\times_QG$ by $(g,p)\mapsto(g,gp)$ and a faithfully flat quotient map $q$. The quotient construction of [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] also gives finite presentation of this map. Its coset-fibre and local-lifting characterization identifies its representing scheme canonically with $Q$ (it is itself an fppf cover, so the local lifts are fppf). Thus $q$ is faithfully flat of finite presentation and is the asserted right $P_I$-torsor.

source.place: Theorem 5.28 and Propositions 5.24--5.27, pp.104--105; Theorem 7.18, p.142; Section 18c, p.390

proof.text: The inclusion $B_0\subseteq P_I$ gives $a:G/B_0\to Q$ by the quotient sheaf universal property, sending $gB_0$ to $gP_I$. It is universally surjective: after every base change, any point of $Q$ lifts fppf locally to $G$ and hence to $G/B_0$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $G/B_0$ is proper over $F$. For any $F$-scheme $S$ and closed subset $Z\subseteq Q\times_FS$, its inverse image under $a_S$ is closed in $(G/B_0)\times_FS$ and has the same image in $S$ as $Z$, by surjectivity. That image is closed by properness of $G/B_0$. Thus $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is universally closed; it is separated and finite type by step 11. The definition [def-weil-proper-morphism] therefore makes $Q$ proper.

source.place: Theorem 17.16 and its proof, p.356; Appendix A.75(d)

proof.text: Put $H=U_{-\lambda}$, using [lem-sfb-cocharacter-limit-smooth-structure] for $-\lambda$. We verify the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-transverse-subgroup-product-open] for $H,P_\lambda\subseteq G$. Their tangent spaces are respectively the negative and nonnegative $\lambda$-weight spaces, and hence sum directly to $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$. Their intersection is trivial on every algebra: for $g\in H(A)\cap P_\lambda(A)$, the orbit $\lambda(t)g\lambda(t)^{-1}$ extends at $0$ and at infinity, and its value at infinity is $1$. For each affine coordinate of $G$, its Laurent polynomial lies in $A[t]\cap A[t^{-1}]=A$. Thus the orbit is constant, equal to $1$, whence $g=1$. Both groups are smooth closed subgroups, so the transverse-product node makes $m:H\times_F P_I\to G$, $(h,p)\mapsto hp$, an open immersion.

Consider $j:H\to Q$, $h\mapsto q(h)$. The torsor identity in [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] identifies its base change along $q:G\to Q$ with $H\times_FP_I\to G$, $(h,p)\mapsto hp$: the fibre product is parametrized by $(h,hp)$. This is the open immersion of step 13. Since $q$ is a surjective flat finitely presented cover, the open-immersion descent statement of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] applies (schemes are algebraic spaces). It follows that $j$ is an open immersion. Write $C=j(H)$. Its inverse $C\to H$, followed by $H\hookrightarrow G$, is a regular section $s:C\to G$ of $q$. The open $C$ contains the identity coset.

source.place: Theorem 25.9(a), p.546; open-immersion descent: Stacks spaces-descent.tex Tag 041X, lemma-descending-property-open-immersion

proof.text: For every $g\in G(F)$, left translation gives the open $gC\subseteq Q$ and the section $x\mapsto g\,s(g^{-1}x)$. Every closed point of $Q$ is an $F$-point by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], and every such point lifts to $g\in G(F)$ by [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry]. It then lies in $gC$. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], a nonempty closed complement would contain a closed point; thus these translates cover $Q$. Finally $Q$ is quasi-compact because its structure morphism is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The definition [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] supplies a finite subcover. All constructions allow empty root sets and $\lambda=0$, so no rank, characteristic or simply connectedness restriction was added.
